title: Chard, cod and new potato frittata

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a whole food or a plain dairy staple: potatoes, chard, spring onions, eggs, crème fraîche, cod, oil, dill and lemon.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is a regular Tesco line, and 300g of cod is an ordinary weeknight buy rather than a treat.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan and a lidded frying pan, and a covered hob frittata is well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: Eight eggs, 400g potatoes, 300g chard and 300g cod make a sensible frittata for four, and raw cod chunks will cook through in 12 to 15 minutes covered on a low heat.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is enough for slicing potatoes, separating and chopping chard, cutting the cod and beating the eggs, and the steps add up to about 25 minutes of cooking.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the dill and the lemon used as zest, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Garden chard in early June is the bulk of the frittata, alongside new potatoes, which suits a light summer lunch.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Eggs, fish, potatoes and greens make a balanced, filling lunch a family would happily eat again.
